services.name: Residential Services and Support for People with Developmental Disabilities
services.description:
To apply, contact the referral and information center. Call 212-780-4491 to get more information on making referrals or contact the Referral and Information Center online at https://www.ahrcnyc.org/ric/contact/. 

Residential supports fall under three models:
1. Individualized Residential Alternatives (IRAs)
Supervised IRAs are traditional family-style group homes, providing 24-hour staff support and supervision for up to 14 residents.
Supportive IRAs provide need-based supports and services for those who are living in their own homes or apartments but do not require 24-hour staff support and supervision. Supportive IRAs are limited to 3 or fewer residents.
2. Supervised Apartments
3. Residential settings for people who are medically fragile (with 24/7 Nursing Care) AHRC NYC operates two residences for aging individuals who require full-time nursing oversight.  Support staff are comprised of nurse practitioners and supervising registered nurses, who are on-site 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.  Residents also have access to speech, physical, and occupational therapies as needed, as well as a day habilitation program operated within the residence.

Monday-Saturday 9am-5pm (syringe exchange 9-4:30).

services.name: Sliding-scale Bicycles and Bike Repair in Brooklyn
services.description: If you are in need of a complete bicycle, email bikeplantnyc@gmail.com with your height, what you will use the bike for, and your phone number, and you will be added to our list. If you're in need of repair, bring your bike to the shop during our regular business hours.

services.name: LGBTQ+ Affirming Mental Health Services

services.name: National Harm Reduction Coalition Resources

services.name: Connections 2026: A Guide for Formerly Incarcerated People in NYC

services.name: Parents' Legal Rights and Information
services.description: This webpage provides links to information for parents related to your legal rights and child welfare and how to get support.

services.name: Affordable Housing through Breaking Ground
services.description:
Offers affordable housing for low-income working professionals and the formerly homeless, some of whom live with HIV/AIDS, mental illness, or physical disabilities.

Call the Central Intake Hotline at 800-324-7055 to request an application, or fill one out online. Fill out a separate and specific application for each building to which you are applying.

services.name: Free food, clothes and supplies in Washington Square Park

services.description: Government ID required. One-time emergency cash assistance, not dependent on immigration status - to prevent eviction, pay energy or utility bills, or buy health-related items. Apply via ACCESS HRA or call (718) 557-1399 for more information. (Processing times *should* be 30 days after applying.)

services.name: Volunteer Program for New Yorkers
services.description: On the website, Bright Light offers volunteering events throughout the city.

services.name: Crisis Toolkit
services.description: An assortment of resources that may provide perspective, comfort, and/or tools that could be of assistance to people experiencing various sorts of tough times. Includes links to informational guides, online peer support, and more.

services.name: Free mental health resources for BIPOC in NYC
services.description: Visit the website to get connected to free resources and tools including "Find Me a Therapist", a Black Mental Health Resource Packet, and a Black Mental Health Provider Database.

services.name: Benefits Enrollment Assistance and Case Management Services in the Rockaways
services.description: Call to connect with services, including a large kosher food warehouse, Medicaid assistance, Medicare enrollment and troubleshooting, SNAP enrollment and troubleshooting, housing assistance, Holocaust survivor services, crisis intervention, support for single mother families, holiday programs and much more.

services.name: Community Fridge in Washington Heights
services.description: Community Fridge in Washington Heights at 181st St & Fort Washington Ave. Take what you need, give what you can. Open 24/7.

services.name: Help for Seniors Accessing Benefits & Support
services.description: Call to make an appointment or find out about a regularly scheduled social work clinics. Connect with case managers for help to access benefits, including medical, financial, housing, and other needs; and get references for legal care and mental health care. Or enroll in the Daily Money Management program to help seniors with day-to-day financial tasks.

services.description: Community fridge in Bushwick always accepting food donations 24 hours /day. DIY don't ask just go.

services.description: Access guides designed to help when you need to go to Family or Supreme Court without an attorney. Provide answers to common questions about divorce, spousal support, orders of protection, child custody and visitation, and child support.

services.description:
What: Homework help line for students and their parents, run by classroom teachers
Where: Call (212) 777-3380

services.description: Information on how to apply for WIC. The WIC program provides support with accessing food, nutrition education, and resources for expecting parents and caregivers. Government ID required.

services.description:
Call the CHAMP live-answer Helpline for free and confidential assistance accessing mental health and substance use disorder care.   Monday-Friday 9am-4pm. Supports multiple languages and all insurance types (including uninsured folks).

CHAMP assistance includes help finding a mental health or substance use disorder provider, appealing an insurer’s denial of care, and understanding your rights to mental health and substance use disorder care.

CHAMP is a partnership among specialist organizations, community based organizations, and the New York State Offices of Addiction Services and Supports (OASAS) and Mental Health.

services.description: Call 1-877-8-HOPENY or text 467369 at any time if you are experiencing substance abuse and problem gambling. This service is free, confidential, and offered in English, Spanish, Bengali, Traditional Chinese, Haitian-Creole, Korean, and Russian.

services.name: Small Claims Court Action Center
services.description:
Get free help with consumer problems and complaints in small claims court, such as the purchase of defective goods, shoddy services, unreturned security deposits, property damage or falling victim to deceptive business practices. 
While the Action Centers don’t provide legal advice or courtroom representation, they can help you resolve consumer problems and boost your chances of success in the small claims courts and with collecting a judgment.

services.name: Financial Counseling and Workshops for South Asian Small Businesses
services.description:
To apply for services, fill out survey on the website. 

Chhaya is a community development corporation with the mission to build the power, housing stability, and economic well-being of South Asian and Indo-Caribbean communities. Chhaya executes this work by providing free direct services in the areas of housing counseling and homeownership, asset building and financial empowerment, policy and advocacy, and community organizing.

services.name: Free Benefits Counseling for People with Disabilities
services.description:
Call 1-844-862-7930 to reach counselors available 9 am until 5 pm, Monday through Friday. You can also request to be contacted by a counselor by filling out the form at https://www.cidny.org/getnyconnects
Support includes SNAP, Unemployment Insurance, Social Security, Medicaid, etc. for people with disabilities and older adults; help getting connected with various resources including food, toiletries, mental health, etc.

services.name: Health and Disability Benefits support for People Living with HIV/AIDS
services.description: Call the Legal Aid Society's HIV/AIDS Representation Project’s helpline at 718-579-8989 if you are a person living with HIV/AIDS and need assistance with a legal matter.

services.name: Sliding Scale Therapy in NY
services.description: Request sliding scale therapy through Liberation-Based Therapy. LBT provides culturally responsive, trauma-informed, and liberation-centered therapy for individuals, couples, families, and groups. Services are primarily virtual, with limited in-person availability in New York City. Sliding scale options may be available based on financial need, therapist availability, and fit. Complete the appointment request form to get connected with the intake team.

services.name: BronxWorks Programs for Elementary School Aged Children
services.description: Access directory of childcare resources including after-school programs, summer camps, and community-center based recreational and education activities for children 5-12 years old operated by BronxWorks.

services.name: Drive Change
services.description:
Drive Change runs an 3-month paid fellowship for formerly incarcerated youth ages 18-25 that focuses on hospitality/restaurant industry training and professional development. Apply online.

To apply, you must be between 18-25, and prove you have 8th grade or higher math and reading level (TABE, GED/TASC or HS DIPLOMA preferred but not necessary).

services.name: Supportive Network for Caregivers for People with Special Healthcare Needs
services.description: Call 1-800-405-8818 if you are working with a parent of a child with disabilities or special health care needs looking for information about support groups and available resources.

services.name: Workforce Training and Supportive Housing for Homeless Men
services.description:
Call Brooklyn: 646-672-2973 | Harlem: 718-417-2538 for more information.
Ready, Willing, and Able is a 12-month residential program with paid work—complemented by holistic social services, career training, education, and sobriety support. If you’re already in the New York City shelter system and would like to join Ready, Willing & Able, talk to your case manager or parole officer about a transfer to a Doe Fund facility. The Ready, Willing & Able program is open to all men able to work and maintain sobriety, ages 18 and up.

services.name: Information About Housing Rights For City Residents
services.description: Information from the NYC Commission on Human Rights about what NYC Human Rights law covers in relation to housing discrimination including specific scenarios in which a complaint might be filed.

services.name: Community and Family Services Counseling and Support
services.description: SCO Family of Services provides a range of community, family, and children's services in Brooklyn and Long Island including access to counseling, community centers, literacy, after school, and employment services.

services.name: Naloxone Access in NYC
services.description: Use this guide to find how to access naloxone in NYC, as well as trainings in how to administer it.

services.name: Legal Issues in Mutual Aid Operations: A Preliminary Guide
services.description: A June 2020 article by Michael Haber about legal issues that impact groups engaged in mutual aid, with a focus on New York. It gives legal information on topics including: risk of liability; questions around governance and incorporation; safety policies, liability waivers, and insurance; banking and mutual aid; funding mutual aid and taxation of mutual aid; crowdfunding regulations; and food storage and safety rules.

services.name: Free Food Distribution Second Saturdays in Jamaica
services.description: Free food and produce distribution at 12pm every 2nd Saturday of the month at the corner of Jamaica Ave and Parsons Blvd, outside of the old Jamaica Multiplex.

services.name: School & Student Rights Legal Support
services.description:
If The Legal Aid Society represents you or your child in a Family Court or Criminal Court case, you can reach out to the attorney to be directed to help with education issues.

If you are not involved in a Family Court or Criminal Court case, you can ask for help with your child’s education needs by calling The Legal Aid’s Civil Access to Benefits helpline at 888-663-6880.

If your child needs representation for an upcoming Superintendent’s Suspension Hearing, please call our Suspension Hotline at 718-250-4510.

services.name: Criminal-Immigration Helpline
services.description:
Immigrants and their loved ones who are affected by the criminal system, including immigrants who have been arrested, ticketed, or convicted of a crime: call the helpline for limited immigration legal advice and information, referrals for free immigration legal services, and referrals for private immigration attorneys. 

The helpline is not live. Leave a voicemail with your name and number at any time and a staff member or volunteer will contact you .

services.name: AfterCare Resource Center for Long COVID
services.description: The AfterCare Resource Center provides information and tools related to Long COVID, and connects New Yorkers recovering from COVID-19 or living with Long COVID to the health and social resources to support them in their recovery. Support provided regardless of one’s ability to pay or immigration status.

services.name: NYC City Government Housing Resource Portal
services.description: A collection of New York City Housing resources, searchable and sortable by topic. Resources include information on legal and financial issues, repairs, safety, reporting problems to the city, tenants rights, and more. Compiled as part of the NYC government "Your Home NYC" initiative.

services.name: NYC Affordable Housing Lottery Application Process Info and Training
services.description:
Go to website to book an in-person appointment at one of multiple locations to receive one-on-one application assistance, including information and training on the necessary interview skills and financial literacy, needed to obtain an affordable housing unit.

There are also a range of referrals available for additional services such as credit repair, tenants rights, legal support, immigrant rights, ELA, job training, domestic abuse assistance, and more.

services.name: Behavioral Health Services for People Struggling with Mental Health and Substance Use
services.description: Reach out via their phone or email for direction to applicable behavioral health services including care coordination, treatment, and recovery: 877-583-5336 or services@sus.org.

12:30 PM - 3:00 PM Monday-Saturday.

services.name: Free Food Delivery for East Asian Elders throughout NYC
services.description:
Deliver weekly hot lunches, fresh produce, and bulk ingredients to East Asian elders while supporting local small businesses.

Fill out the form to join the waitlist. During the next onboarding cycle, they will review your eligibility for receiving Heart of Dinner care packages for free. The criteria:

1. Be a local NYC Asian American person aged 60 or above.
2. Have a gross monthly income as a single elderly at or below $1,869; or have a gross monthly income as an elderly couple at or below $2,518.
3. Unable to prepare meals because of the lack of money to purchase food, inability to shop or cook, or lack of facilities.
4. Isolated due to lack of family, friend or neighbor support.

services.name: Mouse Create: educator resource for free STEM, Design & CS Courses for school groups
services.description: An online learning platform designed for young people to build the tech & design skills. Educators from schools, community centers, and afterschool providers can partner with Mouse to integrate Mouse project curricula into their programs and classes, choosing from courses that cover circuitry, game design, web literacy, coding, green technology, and more.

services.name: Free Food Distribution Mondays and Saturdays in Astoria
services.description: Pick up a pre-packaged bag of groceries Mondays 8am-10:30am and Saturdays 1-1:30pm. No sign-up, id, or name required. 25-82 Steinway St in Queens.

services.name: Covenant House crisis shelter and resources for youth experiencing homelessness
services.description: Any youth 16-21 and their minor child(ren) may go 24/7 to Covenant House NY crisis shelter at 460 West 41st near the Port Authority Bus Terminal. They have beds, clothes, food, showers, laundry, chargers, toiletries, and holistic services. No referral and no immigration status restrictions. States they are a LGBTQ safe space.

services.name: New York City Tenant Resource Portal and Eviction Prevention Tool
services.description: The goal of this portal is to help tenants across the city find the resources they need in one place. This eviction prevention tool was designed by the Mayor's Office to Protect Tenants (MOPT) and the Mayor's Public Engagement Unit's (PEU) Tenant Support Unit (TSU) to help renters navigate public and private resources that can stabilize their housing situation. A tenant seeking help will be taken through a series of questions and directed to the most useful resources based on their responses. MOPT and PEU have included resources from multiple city agencies, Legal Service Providers, and Community Based Organizations.

services.description: Call to learn more. Older adults 60+ can "chat” confidentially by phone for free with a bilingual (Spanish/English) licensed Master’s Level Social Worker, to discuss issues and concerns outside of formal psychotherapy.

services.name: Legal Support Services for LGBTQIA, Polyamorous, and Underserved Families

services.description: Case management program to help adults over the age of 60 in Brooklyn stay in their homes and communities as they age. Email info@heightsandhills.org to learn more and schedule a home visit.

services.name: Sakhi for South Asian Women Helpline for Gender-Based Violence
services.description:
Call (212) 868-6741, text (305) 204-1809, or email advocate@sakhi.org Monday through Friday, 10am-10pm, for assistance with gender-based violence in the South Asian diaspora.

The helpline is able to assist in English, Hindi, Urdu, and Bengali. In addition, they also have an over-the-phone interpretation service if needed for another language.

services.name: Workshops and Programming for Youth
services.description: A calendar of workshops and programming for youth in their late teens to early 20s with the goal of improving the quality of education, health care and life-skills training for underserved adolescents and young adults.

services.name: Interest Free Loans for New Yorkers Seeking Immediate Financial Help
services.description: Hebrew Free Loan Society offers interest free loans for needs such as medical, addiction treatment, higher education, vocational training, and housing. Applicants must be defined as low to moderate income as a household. A government id is required.

services.name: Food Career Training Program
services.description: Apply for this free program on the "career programs" page. This resource is available for women and nonbinary people over 18 who are looking to find a job in food and restaurant services. Must be able to actively take courses for 5 weeks.

services.name: Virtual 12-Step meetings for people who use crystal meth

services.description: For housing services, reach out to the supportive services arm of the organization (631-227-0777 or ssvfintakes@sus.org). For employment, contact 877-583-5336 or services@sus.org.

Housing advocacy in the areas of evictions, complaints, housing code violations, landlord/tenant and tenant/tenant mediation, and dispossession’s and foreclosures preventions. Also provide legal assistance, advocacy on behalf of the client should they be denied, rejected, and/or terminated for the following: housing application forms of HPD/NYCHA section 8, tenancy forms, NYC FEPS application, OTDA FEPS, SNAP, DRIE, LINK, SCRIE, homeowner’s loan program and rent stabilization forms.

services.name: Mercadito Solidario Project

Free and confidential.

services.name: Legal Consultations for Immigrants
services.description: Family-based immigration services including one-on-one legal consultations and application assistance on issues such as: adjustment of legal status, filing for citizenship and naturalization and family-based petitions. Email info@coalitionfreedom.org or call 212-781-0355 ext. 101.

services.name: Silver Corps Volunteer Assignments for Older Adults
services.description:
An AmeriCorps program that provides older adults with volunteer assignments at a partner organization, training, and/or credentialing to secure employment. 

Must be at least 55 years of age, an NYC resident, currently unemployed or underemployed, and commit to volunteering 15 hours per week in a nonprofit or government agency.

Attend a virtual information session by completing the Silver Corps Interest Form linked on the website.

services.name: Food Distribution Tuesdays in Washington Square Park
services.description: Weekly distro of food, hot coffee, and more on Tuesdays 12:30pm-2:30pm in Washington Square Park across from Holley Statue. Take what you want, leave what you can.

services.name: Find an HRSA-Funded Health Center Tool
services.description: Find a Health Center the receives government Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) funding by location. Primary care health services should be available at a reduced cost or free of charge depending on your economic status.

services.name: Mood Disorder Support Groups
services.description:
MDSG is a bi-weekly free support group network for people dealing with a mood disorder. Meetings are Wednesday and Friday 7:30-9:15 over zoom. Groups available include Bipolar, Unipolar, Under 30, and Friends and Family.

A donation is requested, but no one is turned away.

services.name: NYPL Free Online Tutoring for Grades 1-12
services.description: Get free online homework help with your library card from one-on-one tutors, daily from 2–11 PM. Available in English, Spanish, and French from early elementary through high school grades, in core subject areas. Video content and other resources are also available 24 hours a day.

services.name: My Bronx Impact: Find Free or Cost-based Resources by Zipcode
services.description: Enter your zip code to find free or cost-based local resources like medical care, food, job training, education, and more.

services.description: Carefully is a free playdate and childcare exchange platform to build a network of parents you know and trust to share care, redefining the traditional 'care circle' model for the digital age (available for iOS and Android).

services.name: 24-hour Drop-In Center offering free medical and mental health care and services to homeless LGBTQ+ youth
services.description: Call 212.206.0574 ext. 100, or stop by the Drop-In Center at 307 West 38th Street, 3rd floor New York, NY 10018. Open for new intakes Monday-Friday from 8 AM - 8 PM and Saturday and Sunday from 10 AM - 6 PM, except closed Wed 2-4pm.

services.name: Self-Sufficiency Grants
services.description: Emergency grant funding to assist individuals and families who, because they are working and live just above the poverty level, are ineligible for most types of conventional social assistance. Grants are typically between $750 and $1250. Grants come through donors to the national non-profit charity organization Modest Needs.

services.name: New York State Order of Parentage Guide
services.description:
A DIY guide to help non-gestational parents using donor sperm petition Family Court to obtain legal parentage rights to protect their family following the NY Child-Parent Security Act (CPSA). This includes the steps to submit a court petition, example templates, and additional information and resources.

Compiled by a parent who successfully petitioned the court using this process.

services.name: Paid Culinary Job Training Program
services.description:
Fill out application on the website to apply for a free 11-week culinary training program that pays its trainees full time minimum wage. Available for asylum seekers, refugees, and trafficking survivors who have come to the U.S. within the past five years. Offer a chef’s knife and a full uniform, free of cost, to every student.

This program is specifically catered towards people who arrived in the US within five years that were seeking asylum. Must be able to legally work in the US.

services.name: Free Bikes for Fellow New Yorkers
services.description: Donate a spare bike or apply for a free one at bikematch.nyc. Fill out a form, get paired with a neighbor of about the same height, and arrange a time to meet up and exchange the bike.

services.name: Tuition free access to youth dance company (ages 7-18)
services.description: Opportunity for year-long free dance and performance training for youth ages 7-18 at Dancewave (located in Gowanus, Brooklyn). Scholarship application available on the website. Please email school@dancewave.org with questions.

services.name: Therapy and Advocacy for Survivors of Sexual Violence
services.description: Call 212-423-2140. Mount Sinai Sexual Assault and Violence Intervention Program (SAVI) works with survivors who have experienced sexual assault and intimate partner violence. Provide therapy support and advocate for the safety of clients. Located at East Harlem, the Upper East Side, and Queens.

services.name: Lemontree Food Helpline / La línea de ayuda alimentaria de Lemontree

Walk-in center open Wednesdays 7pm – 9pm and Saturdays 6pm – 8pm. We also offer virtual sessions by appointment on Sunday evenings. services.name: Respite Opportunities for Family Members and Caretakers: Out and In-Home
services.description:
Contact AHRC's referral and information center to connect with their staff and make a referral for yourself or someone you know.

AHRC provides respite opportunities for family members and caretakers of a person with a developmental disability who lives in the home with them.  The need for respite care can range from a caretaker needing to go food shopping, visiting the doctor, or simply relaxing. AHRC's respite care ranges from a period of a few hours to a few weeks, also offering programs that engage people with disabilities after their day programs, on weekends and during vacations.

services.name: Temporary Financial Assistance for Families and Individuals
services.description: Temporary Assistance (TA) is temporary financial help for people who are unable to work, can’t find a job, or whose job does not pay enough. The two types of TA are Family Assistance and Safety Net Assistance. Apply via https://mybenefits.ny.gov or file an application at your local department of Social Services. Government ID is required. Call the OTDA Hotline for more information: 1-800-342-3009

services.name: Emotional Support and Crisis Response Hotline
services.description: Call 212-673-3000 to reach The Samaritans of New York completely confidential 24-hour emotional support and crisis response hotline. It's available on an immediate and ongoing basis for individuals who are dealing with every kind of problem, situation, illness, trauma or loss and need someone to talk to who will listen and take you seriously.

services.name: Plentiful App to Find and Make Reservations at Food Pantries
services.description: Download the Plentiful app on Android or text "FOOD" to PANTRY (726-879) from any phone to find a food program and register, make a reservation, or sign up for updates.

services.name: Day Habilitation Program for People with Developmental Disabilities
services.description:
NYC’s Day Habilitation programs are tailored to adults 18 and over. Programs provide diverse services that cater to people’s individual preferences.​

Day Habilitation is available to people with intellectual and developmental disabilities who are over the age of 18, in Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, Staten Island and the Bronx. 

To enroll the participant must have Medicaid, Care manager enrolled in CCO (Care Coordination Organization).

services.name: AARP Social Isolation Prevention for Adults 65 and Older
services.description: Take the AARP three-minute assessment to help you understand your risk level for social isolation and receive helpful information and local recommendations based on your results.

services.name: Benefits Access for SNAP and WIC
services.description:
Call (646) 355-1475 to set up a free, confidential consultation for assistance applying for SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) and WIC (Special Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program for Women, Infants and Children). Hunger Free NYC will go over income eligibility requirements, check to see that you qualify, and then help you gather necessary documents. They also help with the re-certification process. Service in additional languages is available:
Spanish: (347) 599-1510
Mandarin/Cantonese: (646) 935-3513 
Russian: (332) 600-5425

services.description: For youth experiencing dating abuse and domestic violence, access the helpline by calling 800-214-4150 or texting 646-535-DAY1 (3291). Access prevention and know-your-rights resources on the website.

services.name: Eviction Prevention Program
services.description: People in danger of being evicted can call the Eviction Prevention Hotline at 888-850-2712 on Wednesday mornings beginning at 9:30 am. Appointments are limited and first-come, first-serve. To qualify for a one-time payment of $1000 (on average), you must be in court, have a signed court stipulation, and have future ability to pay your ongoing rent.

services.name: Right to Counsel Tenant Organizing Materials
services.description: Tenant organizing resources including a pamphlet and fighting eviction, the case for rent strike, a list of tenant organizing groups across NYC, and Right to Counsel advocacy information.

services.name: Low and No Cost Healthcare through NYC Health + Hospitals
services.description: Visit NYCCare.nyc or call 1-646-NYC-CARE (1-646-692-2273) to enroll in the NYC Care program and access low- and no-cost healthcare from NYC Health + Hospitals, regardless of immigration status. Proof of identity, proof of income, proof of address, and insurance eligibility determination are required. Even if you are unable to provide the required documents, you may still be able to enroll.

services.name: Assistance Fund financial assistance for health-related expenses
services.description: The Assistance Fund is an independent nonprofit organization that helps patients and families facing high medical out-of-pocket costs by providing financial assistance for their copayments, coinsurance, deductibles, and other health-related expenses for over 70 medical conditions (some are waitlist, some are open for application). Find eligibility and more info on the website.

services.name: Peer-to-Peer Food Distribution in Brooklyn
services.description: Sign-up for peer-to-peer food distribution using the online form, and G-REBELS will match people who can offer assistance with people who need assistance. Both parties will receive an email with the other person's contact information, and they can connect directly. Mutual aid might look like: cooking and delivering food to their doorstep, arranging for grocery delivery, or meeting somewhere with purchased food items.

services.name: Home Health Care Services and Assistance
services.description:
A range of home health care services to meet the needs of eligible persons with and without disabilities, including home health aides, personal care aides / companions, nursing, physical, occupational and speech therapies, respiratory therapy, and social work services

To contact or ask questions about home health care services, contact the referral and information center, available 24/7, or visit the office Monday through Friday 8:00 am to 6:00 pm.

Fill out the form to contact the referral and information center. Additionally, they accept fee-for-service and long-term care insurance.

services.name: Online or in-person counseling, health screenings, and additional resources for LGBTQ+ youth ages 13-24
services.description: 1-on-1 counseling via video/phone/chat and group counseling for various needs. Must become a member to access services. Send an email or a text to join@hmi.org with your name and phone number (if you have one) and someone within the organization will contact you.

services.name: Free Counseling and Assistance with Medicare
services.description: Call 1-800-333-4114 to get assistance with understanding Medicare benefits, making enrollment decisions, coordinating Medicare with other insurance, appealing denials of care, determining eligibility for Medicare cost-saving programs, or another topic.

services.name: Free Haircuts
services.description:
Free haircuts for the first 30 clients (with ticket - given at POTS) of all ages.

Come to POTS 2759 Webster Avenue. Starts at 8:30 am – First 30 Clients Tuesday and Thursday.

services.name: Legal support for discrimination for people with conviction records
services.description: The Worker Justice Project combats discrimination faced by workers with arrest or conviction records living in New York City. If you have been denied a job or a license because of your arrest or conviction record and you live in New York City, email the Worker Justice Project at WorkerJustice@legal-aid.org or call 888-663-6880 Monday through Friday from 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.

services.name: Resource List: Food, Health, and Benefits for Elderly People
services.description: A list of resources available to New York City's elderly community, including food, healthcare, and benefits.

services.description: Contact WHEDco’s Home-Based Childcare Program (HBCC) at 347-708-7800. They work with families to help them explore options, determine their eligibility for childcare subsidies, and provide orientation on how to select the right caregiver for their needs. Also offer support services to licensed, registered, and legally-exempt service providers through the Home-Based Childcare Training Program.

services.name: Mutual Aid + Sisterhood Centering Young Black Women
services.description: Connect with YBQ.NYC for free hygiene products, clothing support, food assistance, community events, & mutual aid opportunities for Black women in Brooklyn + Queens. Join our sisterhood-centered community focused on care, empowerment, joy, & accessible support.

services.name: Free Grocery and Supply Delivery

services.name: English, Citizenship Prep, and Community Health Worker Training Classes
services.description:
Complete the online form to apply to Make the Road adult education programs, including: 
- English classes for speakers of other languages 
- Citizenship preparation
- Community health worker training program (Brooklyn only)

For more information, call your preferred location in Bushwick, Jackson Heights, Port Richmond, Brentwood, or White Plains.

services.name: National Hunger Hotline
services.description:
Hunger Free America operates the National Hunger Hotline for people seeking information on how to obtain food. The National Hunger Hotline staff connects callers with emergency food providers in their community, government assistance programs, and various social services.

For English, call 1-866-348-6479
For Spanish, call 1-877-842-6273
Text 914-342-7744
Hours: 7AM - 10PM EST

services.name: National Domestic Violence Hotline

Free hotline and online chat for victims of domestic violence.

Text "START" to 88788
Chat online: https://thehotline.org/

services.name: NYC Financial Justice Hotline
services.description: Call 212-925-4929 for free information, legal advice and referrals on topics including banking, debt, credit, and remittances. Mondays 4-6 and Tuesdays/Wednesdays/Thursdays 12-2. Available to low income NYC residents and community groups only.

services.description:
Free or inexpensive public health insurance is available for those meeting financial eligibility requirements.
Call 1-855-355-5777 to enroll directly or call the Medicaid Helpline (800) 541-2831 for assistance.
Free enrollment assistance through city - call 311 or text CoveredNYC (SeguroNYC en Español) to 877877.
For assistance enrolling through a local community-based organization: call (888) 614-5400 or email enroll@cssny.org.
All NYC Health + Hospitals centers will provide healthcare regardless of insurance coverage, and can help with insurance enrollment: call 1-844-NYC-4NYC.

services.name: SAG-AFTRA Emergency Financial Assistance
services.description: See website for application and eligibility details. Emergency financial assistance is available for SAG-ASTRA members who are in urgent financial need due to an unexpected life crisis such as a natural disaster, accident, health crisis creating a financial burden, loss of work due to an illness, loss of housing due to an eviction, death in the family, or other emergency crisis situations covered under IRS guidelines which pertain to granting tax-free monies to individuals.

services.name: Natural Disaster Distress Hotline
services.description: 1-800-985-5990, is a 24/7, 365-day-a-year. A National hotline dedicated to providing year-round disaster crisis counseling. This toll-free, multilingual, crisis support service is available 24/7 to all residents in the U.S. and its territories who are experiencing emotional distress related to natural or human-caused disasters.

services.name: Temporary Shelter and Help for Muslim Women and Families Facing Domestic Violence, Eviction, or Homelessness
services.description: Call the Helpline at 718-833-2425. They provide shelter, legal and immigration services, help navigating public or government assistance, managing medical needs and mental health resources, assisting in securing long-term housing, and finding employment.

services.name: Source of Income Discrimination (SOI) Mapping Tool
services.description: Explore the crowdsourced map to see how widespread discrimination based on housing vouchers is in a specific NYC neighborhood.

services.name: Supportive housing for adults, seniors, and veterans living with serious mental illness and/or substance use disorders
services.description:
Call 212-663-3000.
Supportive housing. The Bridge houses 1500+ people in the Bronx, Brooklyn, and Manhattan, and offers a range of on-site services based on client level of need, including case management, advocacy, therapeutic activities, and linkages to community-based treatment and services.

services.name: National Dance Institute Free Online Classes
services.description: Platform of free online classes, where NDI teaching artists lead children in signature NDI choreography, a variety of high-energy dance classes for all ability levels, plus exciting music classes. Classes can be accessed at anytime. (Closed captioning is available.)

services.name: Legal Assistance with Employment, Immigration, Housing and Benefits, and TGNCIQ Rights
services.description:
Call a neighborhood community center to access legal support in the areas of employment, immigration law, housing and benefits, and TGNCIQ rights, helping to tackle crises like an impending eviction or an order of deportation.

Bushwick Brooklyn: (718) 418-7690
Jackson Heights, Queens: (718) 565-8500
Port Richmond: (718) 727-1222

services.name: Free legal services for immigrant New Yorkers
services.description:
Call the city-funded, free, and safe MOIA Immigration Legal Support Hotline at 800-354-0365, or call 311 and say, "Immigration Legal," between 9:00am to 6:00pm, Monday to Friday, to get help in any language:

Get answers to immigration policy questions and information on how and where to find help at Legal Support Centers across the City, housed in community sites, public health facilities, public schools, and libraries. Must be a New York City resident and making 200% of the Federal Poverty Level.

services.description: Give what you can, take what you need! Pull up every 3rd Monday of the month on 135th and St Nick to drop off/pick up Clothing Donations for our queer and unhoused community in Harlem & beyond.

services.name: How to Set Up a Mutual Aid Fund
services.description: A September 2020 essay about how the STL Mutual Aid Fund was set up, with tips for other mutual aid organizers.

services.name: Rights Recorder and Chatbot: Report Housing Discrimination
services.description: Turned down by a landlord or broker because of your housing voucher? Record a call and/or report it using the Unlock NYC chatbot and they'll help hold them accountable.

services.name: Support for mothers impacted by the criminal legal system
services.description: Support services for mothers who have been incarcerated including food pantries, thrift shops, supportive housing, job training, educational opportunities, and programming for children and teens.

services.name: Immigrant Legal Support for Survivors of Violence and Abuse
services.description: We help immigrant survivors of violence and abuse obtain status and protection, enabling them to live and work safely in the United States. Our work focuses on humanitarian-based relief created specifically for immigrant survivors, such as U-visas, VAWA self-petitions and asylum, as well as “green card” applications, naturalization, and removal defense. We work with people from around the world who have experienced trauma and offer services in any language.

Resources are available in multiple languages.

services.name: Citywide Doula Initiative to Find Free Doula Services
services.description:
Find professional, no-cost doula services. Check website for contact information for specific doula services by borough. Care is provided depending on zip codes.  To enroll, you must live in one of the neighborhoods shown on the website and be income-eligible for Medicaid. 

The program prioritizes people who: live in a shelter, are in foster care, have no other labor support, are giving birth for the first time, had a previous traumatic birth experience, or have a high-risk medical condition

services.name: Writing Workshops for Teens
services.description: Writing workshops for youth, with free and low-cost options for families who meet income requirements.

services.name: Shelter-Based Clinics for Homeless People
services.description: The shelter-based clinics located in Third Street, Fort Washington, New Providence, and Williams Avenue serve homeless adults from all over New York City. No one is turned away, regardless of their ability to pay. Services include primary care, diabetes testing, depression and substance abuse screening, HIV testing and viral load suppression, tobacco cessation, and detox treatments.

services.name: Pet Loss Support Program
services.description: Free virtual support groups for those who have lost a pet in the last 12 months. Meetings are approximately twice a month on Zoom on Tuesday starting at 6:15 pm. Space is limited and first-come, first-served. Registration closes at 4pm on the day before the meeting.

services.name: Free Clinic Directory
services.description: Free Clinic Directory is a directory of medical and dental clinics and community health centers that can help low-income and uninsured people by offering free and discounted rates for medical and/or dental care. Search by location, name, or phone number.

services.name: Emergency Meal Delivery for Homebound Elderly New Yorkers
services.description:
This resource is only accessible through a case management agency. If eligible, enter address to get the phone number for the Case Management Agency of your district. The Case Management Agency will guide you through the process of getting meals. 

To qualify, you:
-Must be 60 years of age or older
-Must be physically or mentally incapacitated and in need of some assistance
-Must be unable to prepare nutritious meals or have no one to do so for you
-Must be able to live safely at home if services are provided for you

services.name: LGBT National Youth Hotline
services.description: Call 800.246.7743 for volunteer LGBTQIA+ youth peer support hotline. Visit website for hours and one-on-one chat and chatroom options.

services.name: From Shelter to Apartment: A Guide to New York City's Department of Homeless Services
services.description: A foldout poster (English and Spanish versions) that breaks down people’s rights in homeless shelters and the different programs available to help them leave shelter and find affordable permanent housing. It also provides resources on other services shelter residents may have access to, like transportation benefits and storage grants, and what to do when your rights have been violated.

services.name: In-Home Respite for People With Developmental Disabilities
services.description:
For people with developmental disabilities who reside at home with their families, AHRC New York City provides out-of-home and in-home respite opportunities, ranging from a period of a few hours to a few days.

To apply for respite services, contact the referral and information center on AHRCNYC's website.

services.name: Resource Guide for Survivors of Sexual Assault
services.description: A Resource Guide providing a directory of NYC-based organizations serving survivors of sexual violence, sex trafficking, domestic violence, and abuse. Each organization listed has a brief description of its services, contact information, office location, and spoken languages. Resources are categorized by the type of need including helplines, healthcare, financial support, legal options, housing, and more.

services.name: Mutual Aid 101 Toolkit #WeGotOurBlock
services.description: This toolkit includes step by step instructions for how you can build your own mutual aid network. Created in 2020 at the height of the COVID-19 crisis, but contains useful information for other contexts.

services.name: Free Programs and Services for Young People Ages 12 to 24
services.description: The Door offers a variety of services in health, mental health, legal, education, arts, housing, and more for youth and young people ages 12 through 24.

services.name: Fiscal Hosting for Mutual Aid Groups in New York City
services.description: NYC Mutual Aid Groups looking for a fiscal sponsor can get in touch at pactbk@gmail.com. A fiscal sponsor is an entity that holds money on behalf of a collective, and takes care of accounting, taxes, and invoices.

services.name: Empowered NYC: Financial Counseling and Coaching
services.description: Fill out the online form to schedule free one-on-one financial counseling. Help with debt reduction, credit scores, savings, budgeting, opening a bank account, and preparing income information for housing applications. Appointment options may be in-person or by phone.

services.name: Hotline for LGBTQ and HIV-affected Survivors of Violence
services.description: Call 212-714-1141 to reach a free, bilingual (English/Spanish), 24-hour, 365-day-a-year crisis intervention hotline that offers support to LGBTQ & HIV-affected survivors of any type of violence, as well as to those who love and support survivors, including those who have lost a loved one to violence.

services.name: Bronx Community Fridge and Food Hub
services.description:
Take food from the Friendly Fridge Bronx around the corner from the last stop on the 1 train at 242nd St, or leave fresh food to feed our neighbors and use up food unused food. Available for anyone.

Food Hub Hours: Tues, Thurs & Fri at 2 pm

services.name: Crisis Text line: Free text-based crisis counseling
services.description: In the United States, text HOME to 741741 at anytime 24/7 to reach a volunteer crisis counselor.

services.name: Social Service Support at Community Benefits Assistance Centers - Brownsville
services.description:
Walk-in Tuesdays: 10am-3:30pm or call the office.

Community Benefits Assistance (CBA) provides individuals and families with hands-on assistance in applying for public benefits. At our centers, we offer easy access to public services in one place, connecting people to the resources to attain higher education, jobs, and financial stability, legal counseling, help with financial planning, immigration services and referrals to other community-based organizations, as needed.

services.name: Low to No Cost Sexual Health Care, Immunizations, and TB Care
services.description:
The DOHMH Public Health Clinics provide sexual health, immunization, and TB services- regardless of insurance or immigration status. We’re especially focused on making sure care is accessible, LGBTQ+ inclusive, and welcoming for all. If anyone doesn't have health insurance, we offer services on a sliding scale based on income and family size. No income proof is required and no one is ever turned away due to inability to pay.

Clinics are located in Central Harlem, Morrisania, Chelsea, Fort Greene, Jamaica, and Corona

services.description: Call the Crisis Intervention Emergency Hotline at 1-888-358-2384 with questions about accessing shelter or other services, including if you have been denied access to shelter. Leave a detailed message, including your phone number. The Intervention Program is based in NYC and only able to respond to questions regarding NYC services.

services.name: Entertainment Community Fund Emergency Financial Assistance & List of Additional Funds
services.description: Emergency Financial Assistance is available to eligible performing arts and entertainment professionals in times of unexpected critical need and to assist towards basic living expenses such as health care, housing and utilities to prevent eviction or shut-offs. Multiple funds in the entertainment industries are available to apply to, covering a variety of eligibility restrictions.

services.name: Narcotics Anonymous Meetings by Phone and Zoom
services.description:
Both online and phone meetings of Narcotics Anonymous hosted from different countries around the world.
All the meetings on the Virtual NA meetings lists are sorted by language and day of the week.

services.name: VOCAL-NY Syringe Exchange
services.description: Access sterile injection equipment and other supplies for safer injection, fentanyl testing strips, and hygiene supplies. VOCAL-NY is a New York State-licensed Syringe Exchange Program (SEP). Find the Syringe Exchange Team at Douglass St between 3rd & 4th Aves in Brooklyn. May be able to deliver supplies to you through the Peer-Delivered Syringe Exchange (email paula@vocal-ny.org).

services.name: Domestic Violence Hotline
services.description: Call 1-800-621-HOPE (4673) for assistance in domestic violence situations, including crisis counseling, safety planning, assistance with finding domestic violence shelters, and information about resources.

services.name: NYC Mpox Information
services.description: Information on Mpox transmission, symptoms, prevention, and vaccine updates from the New York City Department of Health.

services.name: Resources for fighting the criminalization of survivors of domestic and sexual violence.
services.description: An organization that both offers support, resources, survivor advocates, legal experts, and policy advocates for survivors of domestic and sexual violence, but also organizes around fighting the criminalization of survivors. Provides access to mutual aid resources and joining community organizing efforts to free survivors from the carcerel system.

services.name: Case Management Program for Older New Yorkers
services.description: Call (718) 892-5520 to access the R.A.I.N. Case Management Program, which serves home bound seniors 60 years of age and over residing in Bronx Community Districts 7,8,11, and 12. Case Managers can assess and link seniors to a wide range of services such as transportation, housekeeping, home care, home delivered meals and assistance with entitlements and benefits.

services.name: College Programs for Students with Intellectual Disabilities
services.description: Individuals aged 21 or older with intellectual disabilities who reside in New York City can apply for admission to the Melissa Riggio Higher Education Program at the participating CUNY campus in their borough of residence. To be eligible, applicants must qualify for services from the New York State Office for People with Developmental Disabilities (OPWDD), be enrolled in the Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) Waiver, and have a Care Manager from a Care Coordination Organization.

services.name: New York City Family Legal Aid & Pro Bono Services
services.description: A list of organizations offering family legal aid and pro bono services in New York City.

services.name: Housing Workshops to Learn About Housing Lottery Application Process
services.description:
See website for locations to book an appointment. Receive step-by-step advice on what to expect through the housing lottery application process, including a review of the application and other required documents; information on financial empowerment and managing credit and debt portfolios; and additional support through the selection and interview process. 

In addition to larger workshops, CUFFH also provides One-on-One Application Assistance including information and training on the necessary interview skills and financial literacy needed to obtain an affordable housing unit.

services.name: Clinical Supports, Services, & Treatment for Children and Adults
services.description:
Provides services on a sliding scale fee basis. Services include: Psychological Assessment, Psychosocial Evaluation, Sexuality Assessment, and Additional Assessments, to assess and assist in determining needs for individuals with developmental disabilities. Additional clinical services include: Psychotherapy/Counseling, Crisis Intervention Services, Recovery Supports and Wellness Services, OT, PT, & Speech Services, Nutritional Counseling, and Family Reimbursement.

Clinical Services are available to people with developmental disabilities, ages 5 and up. Additionally, certain support services can be provided to other family members who do not themselves have a disability.

Clinics are in Manhattan (Financial District) and the Bronx (Fordham Heights) and open by appointment only; please no walk-ins.

services.name: Community Fridge in Brooklyn
services.description: Access the Classon Community Fridge, a refrigerator and pantry, on the street outside of Dean Crossfit that is open 24/7 for both food donations and food access.

services.name: Advocacy for Unaccompanied Immigrant Minors
services.description: The Young Center accepts referrals for the appointment of Child Advocates. Fill out the form linked on the website.

services.name: Free Legal Hotline for People with Limited Income
services.description:
Call the Legal Hotline or fill out an online application to connect with staff attorneys who assist callers of limited income on a range of civil legal issues, including matrimonial and family law, housing law, domestic violence, bankruptcy, and debt collection and benefits. Our staff includes bilingual attorneys who speak English and Spanish, and we can accept calls in any language through interpreting services.

The Hotline is open Monday through Thursday from 10am-12pm and 2pm-4pm, and Friday from 9am-12pm.

services.name: Free Monthly Grocery Distribution in Brooklyn

services.name: Help with Moving Expenses
services.description: Assistance for HRA clients related to moving, including help with moving expenses, broker's fees, and NYCHA security deposits. See Special Grant Document Guide webpage for specific forms.

services.name: Free Housing Legal Services & Eviction Prevention Program

Call 718-538-3344 Ext. 100 or 117, Monday-Friday, 9am-5pm.
NAICA's primary focus is geared towards providing legal eviction prevention services to families and individuals who are working, receiving public assistance, or that meet the low-income eligibility and are at risk of losing their homes.

services.name: Free Vegetable Distribution Sundays in Queens
services.description: Free veggie distro every Sunday, ~2:30pm at Roosevelt Ave & 58th St in Woodside, Queens until November 2026.

services.name: Diaper Assistance Program
services.description:
Call 718-402-1212 Mondays between 9:30am-5pm to schedule an appointment for free diapers (walk-ins cannot be accepted at this time). Distribution is in the Bronx. 

To qualify, you must reside with a child 2 years or younger or be expecting (proof of sonogram or official doctors note required), live in the New York City area, and receive WIC and/or SNAP (food stamps). 

Required documents include:
- Photo ID
- Proof of address (no more than 90 days old-electricity bill/light bill/doctors letter/note with client’s name and address)
- Birth certificate(s) for baby or hospital discharge papers for newborn
- WIC proof (WIC app on cellphone or WIC card with a letter/note from WIC office) or Food Stamps/SNAP proof (recent budget letter)

services.name: Community Services for Tenants, Immigrants, Seniors, and Youth
services.description: Asian Americans for Equality (AAFE) works with clients one-on-one to ensure their rights to safe and decent housing, to secure and extend appropriate government housing subsidies, to make sure they have access to social support programs, such as food stamps and Medicaid, and to provide assistance with immigration matters.  Counselors are available in storefront offices in Manhattan’s Chinatown; the Lower East Side; Flushing, Queens; and Sunset Park, Brooklyn. Contact by phone or fill out contact form on website.
